messages.subject: Help me understand the semantics of spread()
messages.subject_clean: Help me understand the semantics of spread()
messages.body_plain:
In this code:

library(tidyr)
dat<-data.frame(var=letters[1:13],value=runif(13))
dat
spread(dat, var, value)
dat$dummy=1
spread(dat, var, value)

Why should the first spread() give me a 13 row data frame (with the values on the trace), while the second gives me a single row (which is what I wanted in the first place)?

Of course, with reshape2 I'd have to specify the dummy explicitly:

library(reshape2)
dat<-data.frame(var=letters[1:13],value=runif(13))
dat
dcast(dat, 1~var, value.var = "value")

... or use the special '.' syntax

dcast(dat, .~var, value.var = "value")

... but even the "..." syntax does what I wanted, and is closest to my first spread() above.

dcast(dat, ...~var, value.var = "value")

I guess my question is why the 13 row data frame makes sense.  Or perhaps it doesn't and I should file an issue?

Best,

-J

messages.subject: Support to possibly melt and cast my data set?? reshape package
messages.subject_clean: Support to possibly melt and cast my data set?? reshape package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to use R to visualize a dataset and need to reshape it first. The data is collected over two months (in day interval); each date a continuous (weight) and a categorical (stage) variable is recorded for each of the 125 individuals (from different groups). And the dataset contains many missing values as the day progresses. I am trying to reshape data set in such a way that it can be used to visualize different stages of the remaining individuals (color coded by groups) across all the dates.

I have created a miniature version of the data set and looking forward to any support. I am wondering if I can do it without splitting the data set for weight and stage in two excel sheets.

Any help will be highly appreciated.

jamuna
